sentences.en: Hello, hello, hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 你好，你好，你好，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 制作的英语学习播客《English Learning for Curious Minds》，在这里你可以聆听精彩的故事，了解世界上稀奇古怪、美妙绝伦的事情，同时还能提高你的英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today is the start of another three-part mini-series, this time on modern Egypt.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天我们开始另一个三部分迷你系列的开篇，这次的主题是现代埃及。

sentences.en: In part one, this episode, we are going to be talking about The Egyptian Revolution.
sentences.zh: 在第一部分，也就是本期节目中，我们将讨论埃及革命。

sentences.en: In part two, the next episode, we are going to be looking at the huge new city Egypt is trying to build in the desert, and ask ourselves whether it is a much-needed modernisation of the country, or a sign of something more sinister.
sentences.zh: 在第二部分，也就是下一期节目中，我们将探讨埃及试图在沙漠中建造的宏伟新城市，并自问这到底是这个国家急需的现代化进程，还是某些更阴暗事情的征兆。

sentences.en: And in part three, we are going to talk about the case of Giulio Regeni, the Italian PhD student who was abducted from the streets of Cairo, tortured and brutally murdered, almost certainly by the Egyptian police.
sentences.zh: 而在第三部分，我们将讨论 Giulio Regeni 的案件，这位意大利博士生在开罗街头被绑架，遭受酷刑并被残酷杀害，几乎可以肯定是埃及警察干的。

sentences.en: OK then, let’s get right into it and talk about the Egyptian Revolution.
sentences.zh: 好了，那我们直接切入正题，聊聊埃及革命。

sentences.en: With the benefit of hindsight, most revolutions look obvious.
sentences.zh: 事后诸葛亮，大多数革命在回顾时都显得顺理成章。

sentences.en: Whether it is an autocratic leader, an unsympathetic elite, widespread famine, police brutality, systemic corruption, high unemployment, runaway inflation, the lack of political freedom or some combination of any or all of these, it’s easy for historians to look back and say, “the conditions were ripe for revolution”.
sentences.zh: 无论是专制领导人、冷漠的精英阶层、普遍的饥荒、警察暴力、系统性腐败、高失业率、恶性通货膨胀、缺乏政治自由，还是其中任何或全部因素的组合，历史学家都很容易回过头来说：“革命的条件已经成熟。”

sentences.en: Egypt in 2011 would have had a tick in the box for practically all of those things.
sentences.zh: 2011 年的埃及几乎所有这些条件都符合。

sentences.en: High unemployment, inflation, police brutality, lack of civic freedoms, corruption, and of course an autocratic leader in the form of Hosni Mubarak.
sentences.zh: 高失业率、通货膨胀、警察暴力、缺乏公民自由、腐败，当然还有以 Hosni Mubarak 为代表的专制领导人。

sentences.en: But Egypt had had all of these, including Mubarak, for three decades.
sentences.zh: 但埃及拥有所有这一切，包括 Mubarak 在内，已经持续了三十年。

sentences.en: The majority of living Egyptians had known nothing else.
sentences.zh: 绝大多数活着的埃及人从未经历过其他的生活。

sentences.en: On the 6th of October, 1981, Egypt’s third president, Anwar Sadat, was assassinated during a military parade.
sentences.zh: 1981 年 10 月 6 日，埃及第三任总统 Anwar Sadat 在一次阅兵式上遇刺身亡。

sentences.en: His assassins were Islamists who did not agree with Egypt’s increasingly close relationship with Israel and held President Sadat wholly responsible.
sentences.zh: 刺杀他的是伊斯兰主义者，他们不同意埃及与以色列日益紧密的亲密关系，并将 Sadat 总统视为全部责任人。

sentences.en: With Sadat dead, blown up by grenades, his vice-president, the then 53-year-old Hosni Mubarak, was sworn in eight days later, becoming president of the Middle East’s most populous country.
sentences.zh: 随着 Sadat 被手榴弹炸死，八天后，他的副总统、时年 53 岁的 Hosni Mubarak 宣誓就职，成为了这个中东人口最多国家的总统。

sentences.en: Mubarak used the threat of Islamic extremism to continue the country’s “state of emergency”, which gave the state heightened powers to arrest, detain, and question if there was even the tiniest inkling of wrongdoing, and in many cases, even if there wasn’t.
sentences.zh: Mubarak 利用伊斯兰极端主义的威胁来延续国家的“紧急状态”，这赋予了国家更大的权力去逮捕、拘留和审讯那些哪怕只有一丝一毫违法苗头的人，在许多情况下，甚至连这种苗头都没有也不放过。

sentences.en: Protests were banned, political opponents were jailed, and the secret police kept a watchful eye on anyone who dared to whisper a complaint.
sentences.zh: 抗议活动被禁止，政治对手被投入监狱，秘密警察则密切监视着任何胆敢低声抱怨的人。

sentences.en: For three decades, Mubarak ruled the country with an iron fist, using the military and security forces to suppress opposition and maintain control over the population.
sentences.zh: 三十年来，Mubarak 以铁腕统治着这个国家，利用军队和安全部队来压制反对派并维持对民众的控制。

sentences.en: To the outside world, Mubarak sold himself as a steady hand, a stable and strong leader in a volatile region.
sentences.zh: 在外部世界看来，Mubarak 把自己包装成一个稳健的掌舵者，一个动荡地区中稳定而强硬的领导人。

sentences.en: Better a friendly dictator than, well, the unknown.
sentences.zh: 与其面对未知，不如选一个友好的独裁者。

sentences.en: And for a while, it worked. The West, especially the United States, propped him up with billions in aid, happy to have a reliable ally who kept the peace with Israel and the oil flowing through the Suez Canal.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，这确实奏效了。西方国家，尤其是美国，用数十亿美元的援助支撑着他，他们很高兴能有一个可靠的盟友来维持与以色列的和平，并让石油源源不断地流过苏伊士运河。

sentences.en: For Mubarak and his cronies, his family and his allies, life was good, very good.
sentences.zh: 对于 Mubarak 及其亲信、他的家人和盟友来说，生活很美好，非常美好。

sentences.en: One estimate put his wealth at as much as $70 billion.
sentences.zh: 据估计，他的财富高达 700 亿美元。

sentences.en: On the President’s official salary of $70,000 a year, it would have taken him a million years to save that much money, but perhaps he was just a canny investor.
sentences.zh: 以总统每年 7 万美元的官方薪水计算，他需要一百万年才能攒下那么多钱，但也许他只是个精明的投资者。

sentences.en: No. He was egregiously corrupt, and he and his allies siphoned off huge amounts of the country’s wealth and stashed it in Swiss banks and foreign property.
sentences.zh: 不，他极其腐败，他和他的盟友掠夺了该国巨额财富，并将其藏在瑞士银行和外国房产中。

sentences.en: Of course, this was at the expense of the average Egyptian.
sentences.zh: 当然，这是以牺牲普通埃及人的利益为代价的。

sentences.en: Like in any highly-corrupt regime, the loss isn’t just the direct loss of money flowing out of the country to off-shore bank accounts.
sentences.zh: 就像在任何高度腐败的政权中一样，损失不仅仅是资金流向海外银行账户的直接损失。

sentences.en: It’s the fact that business is harder, foreign companies don't want to invest in the country; the corruption drags everything down.
sentences.zh: 而是做生意变得更加困难，外国公司不想在这个国家投资；腐败拖累了一切。

sentences.en: And beneath this international façade of stability, the Egyptian people were suffocating.
sentences.zh: 在这层国际稳定的外表之下，埃及人民正在窒息。

sentences.en: In 2011, nearly 40% of the population still lived below the poverty line, scraping by on less than two dollars a day.
sentences.zh: 2011 年，近 40% 的人口仍然生活在贫困线以下，每天靠不到两美元勉强度日。

sentences.en: Young people, who made up a huge chunk of Egypt’s 100 million-strong population, faced a grim future.
sentences.zh: 年轻人占了埃及 1 亿人口的很大一部分，他们面对的是一个黯淡的未来。

sentences.en: University graduates, full of hope, ambition, and qualifications, found themselves driving taxis or selling fruit on street corners because there simply weren’t enough jobs.
sentences.zh: 大学毕业生们满怀希望、雄心勃勃且具备各种资格，却发现自己只能去开出租车或在街角卖水果，因为根本没有足够的工作岗位。

sentences.en: Inflation was eating away at what little money people had.
sentences.zh: 通货膨胀正在侵蚀人们仅有的一点钱。

sentences.en: Bread, a staple of the Egyptian diet, became a luxury for some families.
sentences.zh: 面包，这个埃及人日常饮食的主食，对某些家庭来说已经成了一种奢侈品。

sentences.en: And if you dared to speak out about it? Well, the police were more than happy to remind you who was in charge, often with a baton or worse.
sentences.zh: 如果你敢把这些说出来呢？好吧，警察非常乐意提醒你谁才是老大，通常用的都是警棍或者更糟的手段。

sentences.en: The tipping point, or at least what most commentators see as the first domino to fall, came in late 2010, 2,000 kilometres to the West, in Tunisia.
sentences.zh: 引爆点，或者说至少被大多数评论员视为倒下的第一张骨牌，发生在 2010 年底，2000 公里以西的突尼斯。

sentences.en: A 26-year-old street vendor called Mohamed Bouazizi had been a regular target for Tunisian police.
sentences.zh: 一个名叫 Mohamed Bouazizi 的 26 岁街头小贩经常成为突尼斯警察的目标。

sentences.en: He was frequently hassled and shaken down for bribes, forced to pay money to the police.
sentences.zh: 他经常受到骚扰和勒索敲诈，被迫向警察交钱。

sentences.en: On December 17th, 2010, the police came up to him again.
sentences.zh: 2010 年 12 月 17 日，警察又找到了他。

sentences.en: It’s not clear exactly what happened, and there are varying accounts, but most reports suggest that the police knocked over his fruit cart and took his weighing scales.
sentences.zh: 目前还不清楚具体发生了什么，说法也各有不同，但大多数报道表明，警察推翻了他的水果推车并拿走了他的秤。

sentences.en: With no way to make money and still needing to pay his supplier for the produce that he was planning on selling that day, he went to the local governor’s office to explain what happened and demand the return of his scales.
sentences.zh: 由于无法赚钱，而且仍需向供应商支付他那天计划出售的农产品的货款，他去了当地总督办公室，解释发生的事情并要求归还他的秤。

sentences.en: He had borrowed money to pay for the goods, and now the police had destroyed his only way of earning enough to pay back his debt.
sentences.zh: 他借了钱来支付货款，现在警察却摧毁了他赚取足够资金来偿还债务的唯一途径。

sentences.en: The governor wouldn’t listen. Bouazizi then went to a petrol station, bought a can of petrol, and returned to the governor’s office.
sentences.zh: 总督根本不听。于是 Bouazizi 走到一个加油站，买了一罐汽油，然后回到了总督办公室。

sentences.en: He stood outside in the street, lifted the petrol can up above his head, emptied it all over himself, shouting, “How do you expect me to live?”
sentences.zh: 他站在外面的街道上，把汽油罐举过头顶，全倒在自己身上，大喊着：“你们怎么能让我活下去？”

sentences.en: He then lit a match, engulfing his body in flames.
sentences.zh: 接着他划了一根火柴，全身顿时燃起熊熊大火。

sentences.en: Watchers-on rushed to him and were able to put out the flames.
sentences.zh: 围观者冲向他并设法扑灭了火焰。

sentences.en: He was rushed to hospital, but he didn’t make it; he died 18 days later.
sentences.zh: 他被紧急送往医院，但没能挺过去；18 天后他去世了。

sentences.en: The story of Mohamed Bouazizi spread like wildfire.
sentences.zh: Mohamed Bouazizi 的故事像野火一样传开。

sentences.en: Social media posts, videos, and news reports captured the attention of millions.
sentences.zh: 社交媒体上的帖子、视频和新闻报道吸引了数百万人的关注。

sentences.en: In Tunisia, protests erupted almost immediately, and soon the streets were filled with people calling for change.
sentences.zh: 在突尼斯，抗议活动几乎立即爆发，很快街上就挤满了呼吁变革的人们。

sentences.en: Within a month, Tunisia’s president, Zine El Abidine Ben Ali, had fled the country.
sentences.zh: 不到一个月，突尼斯总统 Zine El Abidine Ben Ali 就逃离了国家。

sentences.en: A dictator who had ruled for 23 years, brought down by the power of a single act of defiance.
sentences.zh: 一个统治了 23 年的独裁者，被一个反抗之举的力量所击倒。

sentences.en: And as the news spread, so did the spirit of protest.
sentences.zh: 随着消息的传播，抗议的精神也随之蔓延。

sentences.en: In Egypt, the frustration and anger that had been simmering for decades were finally ready to boil over.
sentences.zh: 在埃及，几十年来一直在酝酿的沮丧和愤怒终于准备爆发了。

sentences.en: Bouzazi was just like millions of other young people all over the Arab world, struggling every day to make ends meet, with seemingly no way out of the situation, and at the mercy of a corrupt police state.
sentences.zh: Bouazizi 就如同整个阿拉伯世界数百万的其他年轻人一样，每天都在艰难谋生，似乎找不到任何摆脱困境的出路，而且任由腐败的警察国家摆布。

sentences.en: Add to the fire social media - Facebook, Twitter, and YouTube.
sentences.zh: 再加上社交媒体这个火种——Facebook、Twitter 和 YouTube。

sentences.en: These became powerful tools for mobilising protestors, bringing people together and sharing information.
sentences.zh: 这些成为了动员抗议者、将人们聚集在一起以及分享信息的强大工具。

sentences.en: Facebook pages sprang up calling for demonstrations, and videos of the Tunisian protests were shared widely.
sentences.zh: 呼吁示威的 Facebook 页面如雨后春笋般涌现，突尼斯抗议活动的视频也被广泛分享。

sentences.en: One page in particular, named “We Are All Khaled Said,” became a focal point for activists.
sentences.zh: 其中一个名为“我们都是 Khaled Said”的页面成为了活动人士的焦点。

sentences.en: Khaled Said was a young Egyptian man who had been beaten to death by the police, and his story had sparked outrage across the country.
sentences.zh: Khaled Said 是一名被警察殴打致死的年轻埃及人，他的故事在全国范围内引发了愤怒。

sentences.en: Then came January the 25th, 2011. It’s National Police Day in Egypt, a day that commemorates the more than 50 Egyptian police officers who were killed by the British army in 1952.
sentences.zh: 然后来到了 2011 年 1 月 25 日。这是埃及的警察日，这一天是为了纪念 1952 年被英国军队杀害的 50 多名埃及警察。

sentences.en: In theory, it’s a day where the Egyptian people remember and honour the police.
sentences.zh: 从理论上讲，这是埃及人民缅怀和纪念警察的日子。

sentences.en: But this day in 2011 would be marked for a different reason.
sentences.zh: 但 2011 年的这一天将因不同的原因而被铭记。

sentences.en: Through social media, people were encouraged to take to the streets not to support the police but to protest against them.
sentences.zh: 通过社交媒体，人们被鼓励走上街头，不是为了支持警察，而是为了抗议他们。

sentences.en: This was very much a grassroots protest: people who organised Facebook pages, people encouraging others on Twitter, it was not led by any one individual or group.
sentences.zh: 这在很大程度上是一场基层抗议：人们组织 Facebook 页面，人们在 Twitter 上互相鼓励，它并非由任何单一的个人或组织领导。

sentences.en: Still, people came out in their droves. Thousands of people gathered in Cairo, Alexandria, and cities across the country.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，人们还是成群结队地走出来。成千上万的人聚集在开罗、亚历山大以及全国各地的城市。

sentences.en: Their demands, initially, were more about living conditions and social justice than anything else: the right to live a decent life, free from police harassment.
sentences.zh: 他们的诉求最初更多是关于生活条件和社会正义，而不是其他别的：过上体面生活的权利，免受警察骚扰的自由。

sentences.en: It was about fairness, the ability for ordinary Egyptians to feed their family and live without the fear of being extorted or murdered by the police.
sentences.zh: 这是关于公平，是普通埃及人养家糊口的能力，以及无需生活在被警察敲诈或谋杀的恐惧之中的权利。

sentences.en: They chanted for bread, freedom, and justice.
sentences.zh: 他们高呼面包、自由和正义。

sentences.en: At first, the government’s response was predictable – tear gas, rubber bullets, arrests, the textbook response of an authoritarian regime in the face of public protest.
sentences.zh: 起初，政府的反应是可以预见的——催泪瓦斯、橡皮子弹、逮捕，这是专政政权面对公众抗议时的标准教科书式回应。

sentences.en: But unlike previous protests, the demonstrators didn’t disperse.
sentences.zh: 但与以往的抗议不同，示威者并没有散去。

sentences.en: They stood their ground, buoyed by the sense that this time, something was different.
sentences.zh: 他们坚守阵地，受到了一种这次有所不同的感觉的鼓舞。

sentences.en: Tahrir Square, right in the heart of Cairo, became the epicentre of the uprising.
sentences.zh: 解放广场（Tahrir Square），位于开罗的正中心，成为了起义的震中。

sentences.en: Day and night, people occupied the square, camping out despite the threat of violence.
sentences.zh: 日以继夜，人们占领了广场，不顾暴力威胁在那里露营。

sentences.en: Then, two days later, the country went dark.
sentences.zh: 两天后，全国陷入了黑暗。

sentences.en: The largest internet service providers were turned off, as were telephone lines.
sentences.zh: 最大的互联网服务供应商被关闭，电话线也被切断。

sentences.en: Mubarak and his cronies had seen that this movement was being partially facilitated through social media - Facebook, Twitter and YouTube - and clearly thought that simply blocking this, switching it off, would bring about an end to it.
sentences.zh: Mubarak 和他的亲信们看到这场运动部分是通过社交媒体——Facebook、Twitter 和 YouTube——来推动的，显然认为只要简单地封锁它、将其关闭，就能让这一切终结。

sentences.en: It did not work and only served to light a greater fire in the belly of the Egyptians on the street.
sentences.zh: 这并没有奏效，反而只是在街头埃及人的心中点燃了更大的怒火。

sentences.en: As the days went on, the protests only grew larger, with some outlets reporting that a million people had gathered in Tahrir Square.
sentences.zh: 随着日子一天天过去，抗议规模越来越大，一些媒体报道称有一百万人聚集在解放广场。

sentences.en: The government began to panic. Mubarak tried to placate the crowds by promising reforms and reshuffling his cabinet, but it wasn’t enough.
sentences.zh: 政府开始恐慌。Mubarak 试图通过承诺改革和改组内阁来安抚民众，但这还不够。

sentences.en: The army was deployed, but in a twist, they refused to fire on the protestors.
sentences.zh: 军队被部署了，但在一个转折中，他们拒绝向抗议者开枪。

sentences.en: Soldiers and demonstrators mingled, and some soldiers even showed solidarity with the people.
sentences.zh: 士兵和示威者混在一起，一些士兵甚至对人民表现出了声援。

sentences.en: Mubarak’s position was becoming increasingly untenable.
sentences.zh: Mubarak 的地位变得越来越岌岌可危。

sentences.en: The United States, which had supported him for decades, was now calling for restraint and even reform.
sentences.zh: 支持了他几十年的美国，现在也呼吁克制甚至改革。

sentences.en: Finally, on February 11th, 2011, after 18 days of relentless protest, Mubarak stepped down.
sentences.zh: 最终，在 2011 年 2 月 11 日，经过 18 天不间断的抗议，Mubarak 辞职了。

sentences.en: The announcement was made by his vice president, and the crowds erupted in jubilation.
sentences.zh: 这一宣布由他的副总统发表，人群爆发出欢呼声。

sentences.en: The crowds in Tahrir Square danced and cheered, the dictator was gone.
sentences.zh: 解放广场上的人群载歌载舞，欢呼雀跃，独裁者倒台了。

sentences.en: The Egyptians had done it – they had overthrown a man who had ruled their country for 30 years.
sentences.zh: 埃及人做到了——他们推翻了一个统治了他们国家 30 年的人。

sentences.en: But the joy would prove to be short-lived.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，这份喜悦是短暂的。

sentences.en: Toppling Mubarak was one thing; figuring out what came next was a whole different beast.
sentences.zh: 推翻 Mubarak 是一回事；弄清楚接下来该怎么做完全是另一码事。

sentences.en: For several months in the immediate aftermath, the military stepped in to run things, promising elections.
sentences.zh: 在随后的几个月里，军方介入接管了事物，并承诺举行选举。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, political groups that had been crushed under Mubarak, from secular activists to youth movements, trade unions to fledgling political parties, they all scrambled to organise, sensing their opportunity.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在 Mubarak 统治下遭到打压的政治组织，从世俗活动人士到青年运动、工会到羽翼未丰的政党，都敏锐地嗅到了机会，争先恐后地组织起来。

sentences.en: But the problem was that Mubarak had spent decades rigging the game, leaving only token opposition.
sentences.zh: 但问题在于，Mubarak 花了几十年时间操纵这场游戏，只留下象征性的反对派。

sentences.en: And the main opposition, or rather, the main apparent opposition, was the Muslim Brotherhood.
sentences.zh: 而主要的反对派，或者说主要的表面反对派，是穆斯林兄弟会（Muslim Brotherhood）。

sentences.en: This wasn’t exactly a new player on the scene.
sentences.zh: 这并不是什么新面孔。

sentences.en: It was founded in 1928, and had grown into Egypt’s largest and best-organised Islamist movement, preaching social justice through a large network of charities, schools, and mosques.
sentences.zh: 它成立于 1928 年，已发展成为埃及最大、组织最严密的伊斯兰运动，通过庞大的慈善机构、学校和清真寺网络宣扬社会正义。

sentences.en: For years, Mubarak had banned it outright, jailing its leaders and branding it a threat, yet letting it linger in the background as something of a bogeyman.
sentences.zh: 多年来，Mubarak 一直彻底禁止它，将其领导人投入监狱并将其打上威胁的烙印，但又让它作为某种替罪羊在后台苟延残喘。

sentences.en: Mubarak had always framed it as a simple choice: me, the tough military man you know, or the Islamists.
sentences.zh: Mubarak 总是把它塑造成一个简单的选择：我，你认识的强硬军人，或者是伊斯兰主义者。

sentences.en: In other words, better the devil you know than the devil you don’t.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，明知总比未知好。

sentences.en: Now, with Mubarak out of the picture, the Muslim Brotherhood saw its moment.
sentences.zh: 现在，随着 Mubarak 的出局，穆斯林兄弟会看到了它的时刻。

sentences.en: It had a tremendous headstart. Unlike other political parties, it wasn’t starting from scratch.
sentences.zh: 它有着巨大的领先优势。与其他政党不同，它不是从零开始的。

sentences.en: Its decades underground had built a machine no other group could match.
sentences.zh: 它几十年的地下活动建立了一个其他任何组织都无法比拟的机器。

sentences.en: While secularists and youth rallied in Tahrir Square with passion but little structure, the Brotherhood had members, money, and a plan.
sentences.zh: 当世俗主义者和青年们带着激情却缺乏结构在解放广场集会时，兄弟会有成员、有资金、有计划。

sentences.en: Still, initially, it lacked mass appeal.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，它最初缺乏大众吸引力。

sentences.en: Egypt might be a Muslim-majority country, but that didn’t mean the majority of Egyptians wanted to be ruled by an Islamic group.
sentences.zh: 埃及可能是一个穆斯林占多数的国家，但这并不意味着大多数埃及人希望由一个伊斯兰组织来统治。

sentences.en: To try to appeal to a broader population, the group softened its more radical edges, talking more about jobs and fairness than Sharia law, and launched a new political party, the Freedom and Justice Party.
sentences.zh: 为了试图吸引更广泛的人群，该组织软化了其激进的边缘，更多地谈论工作和公平而不是伊斯兰教法，并成立了一个新的政党——自由与正义党。

sentences.en: This wasn’t the Muslim Brotherhood, it was something new, refreshing, and idealistic.
sentences.zh: 这不是穆斯林兄弟会，这是某种新的、耳目一新的、理想主义的东西。

sentences.en: Not everyone bought it. To some, especially the urban middle class and Coptic Christians, it smelled like a power grab dressed up as reform; to others, people who had grown weary of corruption and poverty, it offered hope of a new dawn.
sentences.zh: 并非所有人都买账。对一些人来说，尤其是城市中产阶级和科普特基督徒，这闻起来就像是一场伪装成改革的权力争夺；而对另一些人来说，那些对腐败和贫困感到厌倦的人，它提供了一个新黎明希望。

sentences.en: Polls from late 2011 showed a mixed picture—about 30% of Egyptians backed them, far ahead of any rival, but trust was shaky, with many fearing an Islamist agenda was hidden behind the smiles and promises of prosperity.
sentences.zh: 2011 年底的民意调查显示出一幅复杂的画面——大约 30% 的埃及人支持他们，远远领先于任何竞争对手，但信任并不稳固，许多人担心在微笑和繁荣的承诺背后隐藏着一个伊斯兰主义议程。

sentences.en: Then, in May of 2012, 14 months after the fall of Mubarak, Egypt held its first democratic presidential election.
sentences.zh: 然后，在 2012 年 5 月，即 Mubarak 倒台 14 个月后，埃及举行了首次民主总统选举。

sentences.en: The Egyptian people faced a stark choice.
sentences.zh: 埃及人民面临着严峻的选择。

sentences.en: On one side was Ahmed Shafik, a former Air Force officer and Mubarak’s last prime minister, who promised continuity and stability.
sentences.zh: 一方是 Ahmed Shafik，前空军军官兼 Mubarak 的最后一任总理，他承诺延续性和稳定性。

sentences.en: A safe pair of hands, albeit not so different from those the people had just overthrown.
sentences.zh: 一个稳妥可靠的人，尽管与人们刚刚推翻的那些人并没有太大区别。

sentences.en: On the other was Mohamed Morsi, a softly-spoken former engineering professor and the Brotherhood’s pick to lead its Freedom and Justice Party.
sentences.zh: 另一方是 Mohamed Morsi，一位温和的前工程学教授，也是兄弟会推选的领导其自由与正义党的人。

sentences.en: It was close, but Morsi scraped it, with 51.7% of the vote to Shafik’s 48.3%.
sentences.zh: 这是一场势均力敌的较量，但 Morsi 以微弱优势险胜，获得了 51.7% 的选票，而 Shafik 的得票率为 48.3%。

sentences.en: Turnout was just over 50%, so Morsi won with the votes of around ¼ of the country’s population.
sentences.zh: 投票率仅略高于 50%，因此 Morsi 是靠着大约全国四分之一人口的选票赢得了大选。

sentences.en: The Brotherhood had seized its chance. For the first time, Egypt had a democratically elected president, and Morsi promised a new era of openness and reform.
sentences.zh: 兄弟会抓住了机会。埃及迎来了历史上第一位民主选出的总统，Morsi 承诺开启一个开放和改革的新时代。

sentences.en: But he’d inherited a country on its knees.
sentences.zh: 但他接手的是一个跪倒在地的国家。

sentences.en: Tourism was practically dead, foreign investors had bolted, and bread lines were sparking riots.
sentences.zh: 旅游业几乎瘫痪，外国投资者逃之夭夭，排队买面包引发了骚乱。

sentences.en: Morsi, like many political leaders, found that governing the country was a lot harder than winning the election.
sentences.zh: Morsi 和许多政治领导人一样，发现治理国家比赢得选举要困难得多。

sentences.en: The Muslim Brotherhood had spent decades as an underground movement, organising charity networks and building grassroots support, but it had precious little experience in the business of actually administering a country, and it showed.
sentences.zh: 穆斯林兄弟会作为地下运动度过了几十年，组织慈善网络并建立基层支持，但它在实际管理国家的业务方面经验极其匮乏，而这显露无遗。

sentences.en: To make matters worse, the military wasn’t exactly thrilled to see an Islamist calling the shots.
sentences.zh: 更糟糕的是，军方对于看到一个伊斯兰主义者发号施令可是一点也不高兴。

sentences.en: Yes, Mubarak was gone, but the police and the military were still just as powerful as before, and they were circling like vultures.
sentences.zh: 是的，Mubarak 走了，但警察和军队依然和以前一样强大，他们正像秃鹰一样盘旋。

sentences.en: Then, Morsi made a fatal miscalculation.
sentences.zh: 接着，Morsi 做出了一个致命的误判。

sentences.en: He overreached. In November of 2012, he issued a decree giving himself near-absolute power, claiming it was temporary to protect the revolution from the judiciary, which he believed was still loyal to the old regime.
sentences.zh: 他用力过猛。在 2012 年 11 月，他颁布了一项法令，赋予自己近乎绝对的权力，声称这是临时的，旨在保护革命免受司法机构的影响，他认为司法机构仍然忠于旧政权。

sentences.en: Then came a new constitution, rushed through by his allies.
sentences.zh: 紧接着是一部新宪法，由他的盟友仓促通过。

sentences.en: Secular and Christian groups walked out, calling it an Islamist takeover, and when it passed in a referendum, barely a third of Egyptians voted.
sentences.zh: 世俗和基督教团体纷纷退场，称其为伊斯兰主义者的接管，当它在全民公投中通过时，只有不到三分之一的埃及人在投票中投了赞成票。

sentences.en: To many, Morsi wasn’t building a new Egypt, he was turning it into an Islamic state.
sentences.zh: 在许多人看来，Morsi 并没有在建设一个新的埃及，而是在把它变成一个伊斯兰国。

sentences.en: Protests erupted once again, but this time, they were directed at the new president.
sentences.zh: 抗议活动再次爆发，但这一次，它们的矛头指向了新总统。

sentences.en: The sense of unity that had characterised the anti-Mubarak protests was gone, replaced by deep political polarisation.
sentences.zh: 曾经以反 Mubarak 抗议为特征的团结感已经消失，取而代之的是深刻的政治极化。

sentences.en: All this optimism had, within 12 months really, given way to disappointment.
sentences.zh: 所有这些乐观情绪在短短 12 个月内确实让位给了失望。

sentences.en: And the army, which had craftily positioned itself as a kind of neutral protector, began to reassert its influence.
sentences.zh: 而巧妙地把自己定位为某种中立保护者的军队，开始重新确立其影响力。

sentences.en: By mid-2013, the discontent with Morsi had reached boiling point.
sentences.zh: 到 2013 年中期，对 Morsi 的不满情绪已经达到沸点。

sentences.en: Some polls pegged his approval rating as low as 30%.
sentences.zh: 一些民意调查显示他的支持率低至 30%。

sentences.en: Millions took to the streets, demanding his resignation.
sentences.zh: 数百万人走上街头，要求他辞职。

sentences.en: But this wouldn’t prove to be a people’s revolution.
sentences.zh: 但这并没有证明是一场人民的革命。

sentences.en: The military saw their chance. On July 1st, they issued an ultimatum: sort this out in 48 hours, or we step in.
sentences.zh: 军方看到了机会。7 月 1 日，他们发出最后通牒：在 48 小时内解决此事，否则我们介入。

sentences.en: Morsi dug his heels, insisting he was the legitimate president, elected by the people, which of course, technically he was.
sentences.zh: Morsi 固执己见，坚称自己是合法总统，由人民选出，当然从技术上讲他确实是。

sentences.en: But legitimacy doesn’t mean much when the country’s against you and the army is itching to act.
sentences.zh: 但当全国都反对你而且军队迫不及待想要采取行动时，合法性就没多大意义了。

sentences.en: On July 3rd, 2013, General Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, the head of the armed forces, went on TV and announced that Morsi was out.
sentences.zh: 2013 年 7 月 3 日，武装部队负责人 Abdel Fattah el-Sisi 将军上电视宣布 Morsi 下台。

sentences.en: Morsi, it seems, did not have much of a say in the matter.
sentences.zh: 看来，在这件事上 Morsi 并没有太多的发言权。

sentences.en: Tanks rolled into Cairo, President Morsi was arrested, and an interim government was set up.
sentences.zh: 坦克驶入开罗，Morsi 总统被捕，过渡政府宣告成立。

sentences.en: Sisi, this stern-faced military man with a knack for staying in the shadows, suddenly became the face of Egypt’s next chapter.
sentences.zh: Sisi，这个面容严肃、擅长潜伏在幕后的军人，突然成为了埃及新篇章的代言人。

sentences.en: To Morsi’s supporters, this was a coup, plain and simple: a betrayal of the democratic dream they’d fought for.
sentences.zh: 对 Morsi 的支持者来说，这是一场政变，简单明了：是对他们为之奋斗的民主梦想的背叛。

sentences.en: The Muslim Brotherhood and its supporters organised sit-ins demanding Morsi’s return.
sentences.zh: 穆斯林兄弟会及其支持者组织了静坐示威，要求 Morsi 归来。

sentences.en: For weeks, they held out, but on August 14th, 2013, the military cracked down.
sentences.zh: 他们坚持了好几个星期，但在 2013 年 8 月 14 日，军方进行了镇压。

sentences.en: What happened next was called by Human Rights Watch a crime against humanity.
sentences.zh: 接下来发生的事情被“人权观察”组织称为反人类罪。

sentences.en: Security forces stormed the camps, firing live rounds into the crowds.
sentences.zh: 安全部队冲进营地，向人群发射实弹。

sentences.en: It was one of the bloodiest days in modern Egyptian history, with some reports saying that more than a thousand peaceful protestors were killed by the army.
sentences.zh: 这是现代埃及历史上最血腥的日子之一，一些报道称有一千多名和平抗议者被军队杀害。

sentences.en: The Brotherhood was outlawed again, its leaders jailed or executed, but Sisi didn’t stop there.
sentences.zh: 兄弟会再次被取缔，其领导人被捕或被处决，但 Sisi 并没有就此停手。

sentences.en: Tens of thousands—activists, bloggers, even students—were rounded up in a sweeping crackdown that made Mubarak’s repression look mild by comparison.
sentences.zh: 数以万计的人——活动人士、博主、甚至学生——在一次大清洗中被捕，与此相比，Mubarak 的镇压显得温和多了。

sentences.en: In 2014, Sisi ran for president, winning in a landslide against a token opponent.
sentences.zh: 2014 年，Sisi 竞选总统，在与一个象征性对手的对决中压倒性胜出。

sentences.en: The world watched on with mixed feelings.
sentences.zh: 全世界怀着复杂的心情注视着这一切。

sentences.en: The U.S., wary of losing an ally, avoided calling it a coup, while Gulf states like Saudi Arabia cheered, glad to see the Brotherhood crushed.
sentences.zh: 美国唯恐失去一个盟友，避免称其为政变，而沙特阿拉伯等海湾国家则欢呼雀跃，很高兴看到兄弟会被粉碎。

sentences.en: Sisi had done it, and he has remained Egypt’s President to this very day.
sentences.zh: Sisi 做到了，他至今仍担任埃及总统。

sentences.en: To his fans, he was a saviour, the strongman Egypt needed to stop the chaos.
sentences.zh: 在他的粉丝看来，他是拯救者，是埃及制止混乱所需要的强人。

sentences.en: To his critics, he was Mubarak 2.0: same military playbook, same authoritarian tendencies, just a new face.
sentences.zh: 在他的批评者看来，他是 Mubarak 2.0：同样的军事套路，同样的专制倾向，只是换了一张新面孔。

sentences.en: Protests were crushed, journalists locked up, and that “state of emergency” Mubarak loved so much?
sentences.zh: 抗议活动遭到镇压，记者被关进监狱，而 Mubarak 最喜欢的那种“紧急状态”呢？

sentences.en: Sisi brought it back with a vengeance. The revolution’s dreams of bread, freedom, and social justice faded into the background as stability, however harsh, took centre stage.
sentences.zh: Sisi 带着复仇的气势把它带回来了。革命关于面包、自由和田园诗般的社会正义的梦想逐渐淡出背景，取而代之的是稳定，无论这种稳定多么残酷。

sentences.en: So, after Egypt’s rollercoaster ride from Mubarak to Morsi to Sisi, the country is stuck with another military dictator.
sentences.zh: 因此，经历了从 Mubarak 到 Morsi 再到 Sisi 的过山车般的历程后，埃及再次被另一个军事独裁者困住了。

sentences.en: Is he any better than the last one? Well, that’s a debate Egyptians are still wrestling with today.
sentences.zh: 他比前一个更好吗？嗯，这是埃及人今天仍在纠结的一场辩论。

sentences.en: OK then, that is it for today's episode on the Egyptian Revolution.
sentences.zh: 好了，今天关于埃及革命的节目就到这里。

sentences.en: As a reminder, this was part one of a three-part mini-series on the theme of “modern Egypt”.
sentences.zh: 提醒一下，这是关于“现代埃及”主题的三部分迷你系列的第一部分。

sentences.en: Next up will be an episode on this bold new project to build a capital city in the Egyptian desert, and in part three, we will look at the gruesome but important case of the murder of Giulio Regeni.
sentences.zh: 接下来将是一集关于在埃及沙漠中建造首都这一宏伟新项目的节目，而在第三部分，我们将探讨 Giulio Regeni 遇害这一毛骨悚然但又至关重要的案件。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 您收听的是由 Leonardo English 制作的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，请注意安全，我们下期节目见。
